simple.meaning: אַשְׁמֻרָה (ʼashmurâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a night watch.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַשְׁמֻרָה (H821) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 14:24, with occurrences in Exodus, Judges, 1 Samuel, Psalms, Lamentations.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַשְׁמֻרָה (H821) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַשְׁמֻרָה (H821) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַשְׁמֻרָה (ʼashmurâh) / H821 is traced through Exodus 14:24, Judges 7:19, 1 Samuel 11:11, Psalms 63:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H821. ashmoreth or ashmurah אַשְׁמֹ֫רֶת אַשְׁמוּרָה, noun feminine watch (division of time); — absolute בֳּלּ֑יְלָה אַשְׁמוּרָה Psa 90:4 ; הַתִּיכוֺנָה אַשְׁמֹרֶת ראֹשׁ Judg 7:19 ; construct הַבֹּקֶר אַשְׁמֹרֶת Exod 14:24 (J), 1Sam 11:11 ; plural absolute אַשְׁמֻרוֺת Lam 19:19; Psa 63:7 ; 119:148 .

occurrences.englishText: In the morning watch, Yahweh looked out on the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and confused the Egyptian army.

So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the outermost part of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, when they had but newly set the watch. Then they blew the trumpets and broke in pieces the pitchers that were in their hands.

On the next day, Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the middle of the camp in the morning watch, and struck the Ammonites until the heat of the day. Those who remained were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
For you have been my help.
For a thousand years in your sight are just like yesterday when it is past,
My eyes stay open through the night watches,
Arise, cry out in the night,
